text.p: A lawsuit has been filed against Transitional Hospitals Corp alleging the company failed to make timely disclosure to stockholders that it had received a takeover offer, attorneys for the plaintiffs said Friday.
The plaintiffs in the suit, a purported class action, are Transitional stockholders who sold company shares between February 26 and May 4.
Earlier this week Transitional accepted a $639 million takeover offer from Vencor Inc.

The suit alleges that Transitional was buying shares of its common stock from members of the investing public after receiving a written takeover offer and before fulfilling its requirement to make the offer public.

The suit alleges that the company belatedly disclosed that there had been "expressions of interest" in acquiring it. By that time, merger negotiations had reached an advanced stage, with firm offers made at substantial premiums to the trading price of the company's stock, according to the lawsuit.
The complaint names as defendants the company as well as Wendy Simpson and Richard Conte, identified in the suit as senior executives and directors of Transitional.
Transitional officials were not available for comment.
The suit was filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Nevada. The plaintiffs are represented by the law offices of Jeffrey Abraham.
